Probably not, despite it being geometrically above the horizon.

At your time and location, the Moon is only about **1.3% illuminated** and just **13.2° from the Sun**. The Sun is still **5° above the horizon**, so the sky in that direction is extremely bright, with substantial glare and scattered sunlight. The Moon is also low-ish, at **16.8° altitude**, where atmospheric extinction and haze further reduce its contrast.

A very thin crescent can sometimes be found in daylight by experienced observers under excellent conditions, but usually when it is farther from the Sun, higher in a darker/cleaner part of the sky, or with optical aid. In this case, for a normal unaided observer—even knowing approximately where to look—it would be **extraordinarily difficult and very likely not visible**.

Also, do **not** scan near the Sun with binoculars, a telescope, or unaided staring; at only 13° separation, accidental Sun exposure is a real eye-safety risk.
